newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Telkom seen pressured by new competitor.
newsitem.headline: Telkom seen pressured by new competitor.

text.p: Shares of Indonesian telecommunications giant PT Telekomunikasi Indonesia (Telkom) were likely to remain under pressure in the coming days on reports of a possible new competitor linked to President Suharto, equities analysts said on Tuesday.
Reports in local newspapers named the possible competitor as Jakarta Tower consortium, whose members include President Suharto's brother-in-law, business tycoon Sudwikatmono.
The reports said it could end Telkom's monopoly in basic telecommunications services, but no firm date was mentioned.
Officials of Telkom, which is also listed in New York and London, were not immediately available for comment.
Nevertheless, Director for Post and Telecommunications Djakaria Purawidjaja denied late last week that Telkom was unhappy over the consortium's proposal to offer fixed local and long-distance calls.

"It's not true...that Telkom is not happy (if) Jakarta Tower consortium, whose main business is multimedia, also exploits telephone (services)," Purawidjaja was quoted as saying by Bisnis Indonesia on Monday.
Telkom fell 200 rupiah to 3,625 rupiah, with volume approaching 37 million shares, making it the most heavily traded issue in late trading on Tuesday.

"We all know that Telkom has the exclusive rights to provide local call services until around the year 2011 for short distance calls and 2005 for long distance calls," a telecommunications analyst with a Japanese brokerage firm said.

"If the consortium is allowed to provide the services, it may not hurt Telkom's earnings in the near-term, but judging from Satelindo's experience, it would hurt Telkom in midium and longer term," she said.

Indonesia allowed PT Satelindo, set up in 1993 and controlled by President Suharto's son Bambang Trihatmodjo, to end state-owned PT Indonesia Satelit Corp's (Indosat) monopoly in international telephone services.
Another analyst said Bambang was expected to join Sudwikatmono in tapping further opportunities if the government allowed them to do so, making a formidable force against Telkom.
"Both Bambang and Sudwikatmono have interests in television station SCTV. Both have extensive experiences in the media industry. This is something that Telkom must reckoned with," the analyst said.
Meanwhile, conglomerate PT Bimantara Citra, controlled by Bambang, rose 175 rupiah, or 5.60 percent, to 3,300 rupiah in active trading on Tuesday following the news, brokers said.
